title: Forward Camera ADAS — Lane Centering Performance (P22A0-EXT)
shortDescription: Forward camera based ADAS fault: lane centering corrections are inconsistent or do not match expected steering torque. Stored as P22A0-EXT.
fullDescription: Camera-based advanced driver assistance functions (lane keep, traffic sign recognition, automatic emergency braking) rely on a windshield-mounted forward camera. lane centering corrections are inconsistent or do not match expected steering torque. Stored as P22A0-EXT. The system may temporarily disable lane keep, adaptive cruise, or emergency braking until the fault is resolved.
safetyImpact: ADAS features disabled or degraded; vehicle remains drivable but driver must rely on conventional controls.

causes.cause: Camera lens obstructed by dirt, ice, or sticker
Misaligned or improperly calibrated forward camera
Damaged windshield or aftermarket glass without ADAS bracket

fixSteps.title: Clean Camera & Windshield
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe windshield in front of camera; remove any stickers, debris, or ice that block the lens.

fixSteps.title: Scan ADAS & Read Freeze Frame
fixSteps.instruction: Use bidirectional scan tool to read camera module data, freeze frame, and verify camera identity.

fixSteps.title: Check Mounting & Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect bracket; perform static or dynamic calibration with OEM target after windshield work.

fixSteps.title: Replace Camera Module
fixSteps.instruction: If calibration fails, replace forward camera and recalibrate per OEM procedure.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Yes, but ADAS features will be limited. Drive cautiously and schedule service.

faq.q: Does a windshield replacement require recalibration?
faq.a: Yes — most ADAS-equipped vehicles require static or dynamic camera recalibration after glass work.

title: Steering Torque Sensor — main signal out of range high (C2400-EXT)
shortDescription: Electric power steering torque sensor circuit fault: main signal out of range high. Stored as C2400-EXT.
fullDescription: The torque sensor on the steering column reports driver input to the EPS module so it can apply assist and feed lane keep steering corrections. main signal out of range high. Stored as C2400-EXT. A bad signal causes loss of assist, uneven assist, or loss of lane keep functionality.
safetyImpact: Loss of power steering assist results in heavy steering, especially at low speed; reduces ADAS lane keep accuracy.

causes.cause: Failed torque sensor in steering column
Open or shorted torque sensor circuit
EPS module software needs update or reflash

symptoms: Loss of assist at low speed

fixSteps.title: Scan EPS Module
fixSteps.instruction: Read EPS codes and live torque sensor data; check for signal at center, left, and right.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check torque sensor connector for corrosion, bent pins, broken wires near the column.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Output
fixSteps.instruction: Compare torque signal to spec; both signals should mirror across center.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor or Column
fixSteps.instruction: Replace torque sensor or full column assembly; relearn steering angle and torque zero point.

faq.q: Can a low battery cause this?
faq.a: Yes — EPS modules will set torque sensor codes during cranking with low voltage. Charge battery first.
Most vehicles require steering angle and torque zero relearn after sensor replacement.

title: Yaw Rate Sensor — yaw rate signal stuck at zero (C0061-EXT)
shortDescription: Yaw rate / lateral acceleration sensor fault: yaw rate signal stuck at zero. Stored as C0061-EXT.
fullDescription: The yaw rate sensor (often combined with lateral and longitudinal accelerometers in one IMU under the center console) feeds the stability control, ADAS, and rollover modules. yaw rate signal stuck at zero. Stored as C0061-EXT. A faulty signal disables ESC, traction control, and most ADAS lateral functions.
safetyImpact: ESC, traction control, and ADAS lateral functions disabled — vehicle has reduced loss-of-control protection.

causes.cause: Sensor moved or unsecured under console
Sensor needs zero-point calibration after wheel alignment

fixSteps.title: Verify Sensor Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Locate IMU under center console or seat; ensure all mounting bolts are tight and sensor is flat.

fixSteps.title: Check CAN Communication
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to verify yaw rate, lateral, and longitudinal acceleration values at standstill (should be near zero).

fixSteps.title: Perform Zero-Point Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Run OEM zero-point reset on level surface with wheels straight.

fixSteps.title: Replace IMU
fixSteps.instruction: If calibration fails, replace yaw rate sensor; recalibrate steering angle and yaw at the same time.

faq.a: Many vehicles require yaw and steering angle reset after toe adjustment or strut work.
Yes — adaptive cruise typically requires valid yaw signal.

title: ADAS Driver Interface — haptic seat motor driver fault (B2700-EXT)
shortDescription: ADAS driver interface / HMI fault: haptic seat motor driver fault. Stored as B2700-EXT.
fullDescription: ADAS HMI codes cover the warning chime amplifier, head-up display, haptic seat motor, and steering-wheel buttons that the driver assistance system uses to alert the driver. haptic seat motor driver fault. Stored as B2700-EXT. The driver may receive missing or incorrect alerts even when the ADAS sensors operate correctly.
safetyImpact: Reduced or missing driver alerts; ADAS features remain active but warnings may be silent or visual only.

causes.cause: Failed haptic seat motor or HUD projector

fixSteps.title: Verify Driver Settings
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm ADAS warning method (audible, visual, haptic) is enabled in vehicle menu.

fixSteps.title: Scan ADAS & HMI Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Read codes from ADAS controller and HMI subsystem; check freeze frame.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect haptic seat connector or HUD harness; look for damaged wiring after seat removal.

fixSteps.title: Reflash or Replace HMI Device
fixSteps.instruction: Apply OEM software update; replace haptic motor or HUD projector if commanded test fails.

faq.a: Yes — many vehicles allow choosing audible-only or visual-only alerts.
No, HMI devices do not require ADAS recalibration.

title: Brake Force Monitor — pedal force signal high (C1300-EXT)
shortDescription: Brake force / pedal force sensor fault: pedal force signal high. Stored as C1300-EXT.
fullDescription: Modern stability control and adaptive cruise systems use a brake pedal force or master cylinder pressure sensor to monitor driver braking effort and to coordinate with autonomous emergency braking. pedal force signal high. Stored as C1300-EXT. A faulty signal disables AEB and may degrade hill-hold and trailer brake functions.
safetyImpact: Autonomous emergency braking degraded; conventional brakes work normally. Hill-hold and trailer functions may be limited.

causes.cause: Failed pedal force or pressure sensor
Master cylinder leak affecting pressure signal
Brake fluid contamination on pressure sensor

fixSteps.title: Scan Brake & ADAS Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Read codes; verify master cylinder pressure reads near 0 with pedal up and rises with pedal applied.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor connector at master cylinder or pedal box for fluid contamination and corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Bleed Brakes
fixSteps.instruction: Bleed at all calipers; ensure no air at pressure sensor mounting boss.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace pressure sensor; perform brake-pedal travel learn and ESC calibration.

faq.a: Yes — base hydraulic braking is unaffected. Only the assist functions degrade.
Recommended any time a hydraulic pressure sensor is removed.
